To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the TORC2 signaling cascade is stimulated in response acetic acid stress, 2) TORC2-YPK1-mediated sphingolipd biosynthesis is required for acitic acid tolerance, 3) sphingolipds produced during acetic acid stress contribute to acetic acid tolerance.
TORC2 signaling is stimulated by acetic acid, and that the resulting activation of Ypk1 is necessary for tolerance to this stress.

TORC2 and Ypk1 are required for tolerance to acetic-acid stress in yeast, that TORC2 activation of Ypk1 is required for tolerance to this stress, and that sphingolipd production contributes to tolerance to acetic acis stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying yeast adaptation to acetic acid, a major inhibitor of industrial fermentations.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the adaptation of the model yeast Saccharomyces to acetic acid, a stressor of great relevance in industrial biotechnology.
the cellular mechanisms that allow yeasts to survive and grow in the presence of acetic acid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the TORC2 signaling pathway, through its activation of the Ypk1 kinase and the subsequent activation of sphingoliphospholipid biosynthetic enzymes, contributes to acetic acid tolerance in Saccharomycescerevisiae.
the TORC2 pathway is required for acetyl acid tolerance and that the TORC-Ypk1 pathway is involved in the regulation of sphingoliphid biosynthesis, which is required for acetylic acid tolerance.
TORC2 signaling regulates sphingolipd biosynthesis in response to acitic acid stress, and that sphingolipds contribute to acitic acid tolerance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TORC2 signaling plays an important role in acetic acid tolerance in yeast, and that this is achieved by upregulation of sphingoligd biosynthesis.

acetic acid stress induces TORC2-YPK1 signaling and that TORC2-activated YPK1 phosphorylates sphingolipin kinase 1 (SLK1), the enzyme that catalyzes a rate-limiting step of sphingosine biosynthesis and is required for the production of complex sphingolips, which are required for acetic stress tolerance.
TORC2 activation by acetic acid leads to Ypk1 phosphorylating sphingolipin synthetase, which increases the synthesis of complex sphingolips that contribute to acetic acid tolerance in yeast.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sphingolipidosome synthesis, and not the synthesis of the major sphingolipidis, ceramide, is the key determinant of yeast acetic acid stress resistance.
TORC2 signaling and Ypk1 activation are required for acetic-acid tolerance in S. cerevisiae.

the TOR complex 2 ( TORC2 )- Ypk1 signaling pathway plays a critical role in the adaptation of Saccharomyces  c erevisiae  cells to acetic acid and that it does so through the regulation of sphingol ip id synthesis.
